name: Buamu
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Manessy, Gabriel. 1960. Le bwamu et ses dialectes (IFAN, Dakar); descriptive coverage of Bwamu/Buamu, not found online.

sources.citation: Yé, Dofissan Alban. 2023-2024. Une bibliographie chronologique du Buamu. Villeurbanne. 21 pp.
sources.note: Bibliography only; used to identify Bicaba 2020 thesis, Bolli et al. 1981, Pfurtscheller 2012, Zongo 1989, Dakuyo 1985/1989, Diarra 1994, Malgoubri 2020.

sources.citation: Pfurtscheller, Lisa. 2012. Esquisse du système tonal du bwamu laa (langue gur du Burkina Faso). Diplomarbeit, Universität Wien. 183 pp. doi:10.25365/thesis.19113
sources.note: Sister variety Bwamu Laa [bwj]: three phonological tone levels H, M, B (p.49, quoting Manessy 1961:127 for Bwamu dialects generally: 'trois tons ponctuels : haut, moyen, bas'); on accent only p.95: 'Il faut encore étudier en détail l'interaction des tons, de l'accent du bwamu laa (s'il y en a) et de l'accent français' — i.e. word accent undescribed; French loanword stress is borrowed as H tone.

sources.citation: Riccitelli, James M. 1965. Tone analysis: a practical approach. The Bible Translator 16(2): 54-73.
sources.note: Tone only: 'Bwamu is a four-tone language' (p.69), tone sandhi rules; stress mentioned only as an English analogy. Dialect not named (author worked in Mali; probably Bomu).

sources.citation: Bicaba, Roland. 2026. Du statut des prédicatifs dits verbaux en buamu (langue gur). Language Policy in Africa 2(1): 240-250. doi:10.36950/lpia-02-01-2026-13
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. Data are tone-marked (H/M/L); p.243: 'Lorsque le verbe monosyllabique porte un ton moyen, la voyelle alternée se nasalise.' Describes the 'tē' parler of Bondoukuy commune (= Buamu central dialect).

sources.citation: Bicaba, Roland & Abel Ouedraogo. 2025. Postpositions et détermination en buamu (langue gur). Akofena 17(5): 233-240.
Traoré, Margueritte-Marie. 2025. Étude comparative du lexique des dialectes du buamu: cas des parlers de Bomborokuy et de Koumbia. Akofena hors-série 12: 71-76.
sources.note: Gives consonant/vowel inventories of two parlers only; nothing on tone or stress.

sources.citation: Bicaba, Roland & Parfait Babine. 2022. Relativisation en buamu, langue gur. Akofena spécial 9(1): 39-48.
sources.note: Nothing; syntax only. Cites Bicaba 2020a 'Phonologie et morphosyntaxe du buamu (Parler de Ouakara)', Thèse UJKZ, 403 p.

sources.citation: Bicaba, Roland. 2022 [Djiboul spécial 6, Feb. 2023 print]. Dérivation et détermination en buamu (langue gur). Djiboul spécial 6: 42-51.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; tone-marked morphology data of the central 'tē' dialect.

sources.citation: Kohoun, Lamoussahan dite Sara. 2021. La dérivation affixale en bwamu [parler de Poundou]. Djiboul 2(4): 280-293.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; notes tonal schemes of bases (cvv, cvn) and tonal alternations bas~moyen, moyen~haut on the final vowel under suffixation. Poundou parler (Mouhoun province, Manessy's 'dialectes du sud-est').

sources.citation: SIL language resource page for Buamu [box] (2015 Wayback snapshot) and SIL archive entry 9230
sources.note: Only literacy booklets and the 2001 survey listed; no phonology/orthography statement archived as of 2015. Live sil.org blocked by Cloudflare from our machine.

sources.citation: Berthelette, John & Carol Berthelette. 2001. Sociolinguistic survey report for the Bwamu language. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2001-006.
sources.note: Nothing; survey. Notes SIL team (Thomson, Allen, Viinikkala) 'currently preparing a paper on this [Ouarkoye] dialect's phonology' and lists Zongo 1989, Dakuyo 1989, Diarra 1994, Bolli et al. 1981 phonologies.

sources.citation: Millogo, Louis. 2001. Ancrage culturel africain d'un roman d'expression française: la langue bwamu dans Crépuscule des temps anciens du Burkinabè Nazi Boni. Thèse d'État, Université de Ouagadougou. 449 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; discusses Nazi Boni's French-based spelling of Bwamu words (searched scanned text for accent/ton/phonologie).

sources.citation: Manessy, Gabriel. 1961. Le bwamu et ses dialectes. Bulletin de l'IFAN, série B, 23(1-2): 119-178 [= Publications de la Section de Langues et Littératures 9, Université de Dakar].
